**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: A single sugarcane leaf blade laid flat
- **Color pattern**: Broad tan/straw-yellow discoloration spanning most of the leaf width, with a narrow green band retained along the central midrib area; the tip end shows more orange-brown progression
- **Texture/pattern**: The discoloration is diffuse and longitudinal — no discrete spots, no mosaic mottling, no streak lines; the transition from green (center) to yellow-tan (margins) runs parallel to the leaf veins
- **Distribution**: The yellowing/scalding dominates the lamina on both sides of the midrib, leaving only the central stripe green

**Reasoning through candidates:**
- **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete lesions or spots visible
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus / Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Ruled out — no mosaic/mottling or streak pattern
- **Grassy_Shoot / Sett_Rot / Pokkah_Boeng**: Ruled out — those affect growth point/stems, not a flat leaf like this
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Yellow leaf disease yellows the midrib first (especially abaxially); here the midrib remains the *greenest* part while margins are affected
- **Leaf_Scald**: Caused by *Xanthomonas albilineans* — classically produces cream-to-tan/straw coloring running parallel to veins from the leaf margins inward, with residual green along the midrib. The broad, longitudinal, scalded appearance with green central retention matches precisely.
